name: Sucrose Esters & Sucroglycerides
aliases: E473, E474, sucrose esters, sucrose esters of fatty acids, sucrose fatty acid esters, sucroglycerides
what_is: Emulsifiers made from sucrose and fatty acids. E473 is sucrose esters of fatty acids; E474 is sucroglycerides.
why_botia: Sucrose esters are made by joining sugar and fatty acids and are used to keep fat and water mixed. The body breaks them down into their components. JECFA set a group ADI of 0–30 mg/kg body weight because higher doses can have a laxative effect. In its conservative 2020 estimate, high exposure in children aged 3–9 reached 113 mg/kg per day, almost four times that limit; JECFA considered the estimate conservative and asked for more refined exposure calculations.
can_1: Detect E473, E474, sucrose esters of fatty acids and sucroglycerides.
can_2: Explain the JECFA group ADI and that the 2020 conservative high-exposure estimate exceeded it in children aged 3–9.
cannot_1: Determine how much E473 or E474 is present in a product from the ingredient list.
cannot_2: Treat a conservative population exposure estimate as proof that an individual child consuming a particular product exceeds the ADI.

title: Sucrose Esters & Sucroglycerides
description: Sucrose esters E473 and sucroglycerides E474 are emulsifiers with a JECFA group ADI of 0–30 mg/kg body weight. A conservative 2020 exposure estimate exceeded that value in children.
